data.narrative:
Last Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Bret Kugelmass that has raised $140M+, operates within a frontier sector where reliable comparables are constrained. The valuation universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private competitors, though peer-median methodology proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow nuclear energy cohort.

Stage-progression analysis, the only applicable triangulation method, anchors valuation to the $140M total raised proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-round advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $238M. The median reflects this single-method result, with the range bounded by low of $202M and high of $274M, representing sensitivity around the core 1.7x multiplier assumption.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $238M, with a plausible range of $202M–$274M. Key uncertainties include: (1) absence of direct-stage peer data limiting cross-validation; (2) whether the 1.7x step-up adequately reflects Last Energy's specific capital efficiency and technology maturity relative to stage peers; and (3) sector-wide regulatory and commercialization risk not captured in stage-based mechanics. Additional datapoints on recent Series C rounds within advanced nuclear would strengthen conviction.
